subject: Initial wake delay causing p95/p99 regressions — Bluefin Pay production
messages:
From: Sara Cho <sara.cho@bluefinpay.com>
To: support@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sharp spike in response times + 504s on hosted API - urgent

Hi Redwood team,

We started seeing a massive jump in p95/p99 response times and a handful of 504s on our production integration around 08:50 PST. Traffic hasn't changed on our side — you can see a spike in latency in the attached sample.

Details:
- p95 rose from ~650ms to ~3.2s, p99 to ~11s for text.generate endpoints
- Error rate jumped to ~3% (HTTP 504) between 08:50–09:20
- Impact: checkout flows retrying; revenue impact beginning at ~08:57

We need immediate confirmation if this is a Redwood service-side issue and what mitigation steps you can take (routing, model fallback, capacity pinning). Please escalate to engineering and let me know ETA for a mitigation.

Attached: p99-extract-0211.csv (sample request/response latencies)

Sara
Sara Cho
Head of Integrations, Bluefin Pay
ops@bluefinpay.com

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Cho <sara.cho@bluefinpay.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>, support@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 09:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sharp spike in response times + 504s on hosted API - urgent

Sara — thank you for the quick heads up and sample. I’m very sorry for the disruption. We’ve opened SUP-7291 and triaged as high priority: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-7291

Immediate actions (underway):
- Triage & telemetry: engineering is pulling end-to-end traces and host-level metrics (attached initial-telemetry-snapshot.json).
- Routing mitigation: attempting a short routing shift to a warmer GPU pool for Bluefin traffic to reduce cold-starts (will update in ~15m).
- CS/engineering sync: Priya is on the incident and will coordinate fixes; I’ve looped in Markus (engineering leadership) for exec visibility.

Could you share whether the traffic pattern includes any sudden burst (e.g., batch job) and whether you can tolerate a temporary model variant (smaller quantized model) for a % of traffic while we stabilize? That fallback reduces cold-init overhead.

I’ll update every 15 minutes until stable.

— Logan Wright
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Sara Cho <sara.cho@bluefinpay.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 09:35:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sharp spike in response times + 504s on hosted API - urgent

On Thu, Feb 11, 2027 at 09:20 AM Logan Wright wrote:
> Immediate actions (underway): triage & telemetry, routing mitigation, CS/engineering sync.

Update from the infra/serving side: we are seeing a clear pattern consistent with cold-start penalties on autoscaling GPU pools for Hosted API. Summary:
- Observed: p99 jumps from ~800ms baseline to 10–13s during scale events; p95 moves to 2–4s.
- Time window: 08:50–09:22 peak; a smaller recurrent blip at 09:28.
- Error mode: 504s appear correlated with short-lived request queue timeouts while new instances boot and accept requests.
- Suspect root cause: a recent autoscaler parameter change increased aggressive scale-downs (min_capacity set to 0 for some customer pools) plus a small regression in warmup signaling.

Immediate mitigations executed (09:30):
- Pinned minimum pool capacity for Bluefin to 2 instances for the next 90 minutes to guarantee warm nodes.
- Triggered explicit warmup RPCs to rebuild KV cache for active models.
- Temporarily enabled soft-queueing for requests to avoid hard 504s while instances finish init.

We expect initial latency improvement within 10–20 minutes; a full return to baseline when all pools are warmed (~30–45 minutes). Attaching metrics-screenshot.png showing the p99 curve.

Next steps:
- Roll back the last autoscaler PR that relaxed min_capacity until we ship a safer policy.
- Create a targeted hotfix to reduce cold-init time by optimizing model load paths (ETA for hotfix: ~2 hours).
- Post-incident: full postmortem and compensatory credit if SLA impacted.

Will keep you posted — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Cho <sara.cho@bluefinpay.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sharp spike in response times + 504s on hosted API - urgent

Thanks for the rapid response. We appreciate the pinning and warmup attempts — we’re seeing some improvement but still intermittent timeouts on checkout endpoints (sample log below).

> [2027-02-11T09:58:23Z] 504 host=api.redwood.ai path=/v1/text.generate latency=11012ms request_id=abc123

We need:
- A named executive contact for Bluefin while this is active
- ETA on the hotfix and whether you will proactively route traffic for us if the pattern resumes
- Clarification on credits & SLA remediation (this spike spans 28 minutes at production impact)

Please escalate.

Sara
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Cho <sara.cho@bluefinpay.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, execs@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 16:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sharp spike in response times + 504s on hosted API - urgent

Sara & team — I’m Markus (VP, Serving Infrastructure). First, apologies for the user impact. We own this and will ensure Bluefin has a named contact through resolution (Avery Johnson will be the primary).

Immediate commitments:
- Mitigation: we have left min_capacity=2 for Bluefin and will keep it for 24 hours while we validate stability. We’ve also routed 20% of your traffic to a lower-latency quantized fallback model to reduce tail.
- Hotfix: engineering will deploy a targeted change to the autoscaler warmup behavior to reduce cold boot penalty (ETA: 2 hours). If we observe additional spikes we will enact an automated routing shift to Dedicated-like warm pools for your traffic.
- Credits: we will issue a one-week service credit for the impacted window and will include this incident in your SLA remediation request.
- Postmortem: full timeline and root cause analysis (including the PR that relaxed min_capacity) will be delivered within 72 hours. Draft will be posted to: https://drive.redwood.net/teams/eng/bluefin-postmortem-draft

Attached: action-plan-brief.pdf (summary of mitigations & timelines).

We will follow up in this thread and with direct outreach. Again, sorry — we are treating this with exec attention.

— Markus Klein
VP, Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
